name: Morgan Stanley

summary.text: Morgan Stanley is a New York-based investment bank. On September 21, 2008 the Federal Reserve Board approved its application, alongside Goldman Sachs's, to become a bank holding company, giving it ongoing access to the discount window; it received $10 billion under the TARP Capital Purchase Program in October 2008 and repaid it in June 2009. In March 2021 it was one of the prime brokers to Archegos Capital Management: it sold about $5 billion of Archegos-related shares on the evening of March 25, 2021 and reported $911 million of related losses, while Credit Suisse and Nomura absorbed far larger losses. Archegos founder Bill Hwang was convicted in July 2024 and sentenced to 18 years in prison.

facts.claim: On September 21, 2008 the Federal Reserve Board approved the applications of Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley to become bank holding companies, pending a statutory five-day antitrust waiting period, and authorized the New York Fed to extend credit to the London broker-dealer subsidiaries of Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch; on September 22 the Board said the transactions could be consummated immediately.
facts.quote: Board approves, pending a statutory five-day antitrust waiting period, the applications of Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley to become bank holding companies

facts.claim: Morgan Stanley's 2008 annual report says the bank holding company status provides it ongoing access to the Federal Reserve Bank discount window and expanded funding opportunities, and that in October 2008 the Treasury announced its intention to inject capital into nine large U.S. financial institutions, including Morgan Stanley, under the TARP Capital Purchase Program.
facts.quote: the U.S. Treasury announced its intention to inject capital into nine large U.S. financial institutions, including the Company, under the TARP Capital Purchase Program in October 2008

facts.claim: CNBC reported that on the evening of Thursday March 25, 2021 Morgan Stanley sold about $5 billion of Archegos-related shares at a discount to a small group of hedge funds, telling them the shares were part of a margin call that could prevent the collapse of an unnamed client, ahead of block sales by other banks the next day.
facts.quote: Morgan Stanley sold about $5 billion of Archegos-related shares to a small group of hedge funds late on Thursday, March 25.

facts.claim: Morgan Stanley reported $911 million of first-quarter 2021 losses tied to Archegos: a $644 million loss from a credit event representing what the client owed under the transactions and failed to pay, plus $267 million in related trading losses.
facts.quote: That resulted in a net loss of $644 million which represents the amount the client owed us under the transactions that they failed to pay us.

facts.claim: CNBC reported that Goldman Sachs sold most of the stock related to its Archegos margin calls on Friday March 26, 2021 and avoided losses, while Credit Suisse took a hit of more than $4.7 billion and Nomura about $2.9 billion; global banks' Archegos losses were later put at more than $10 billion.
facts.quote: Goldman managed to sell most of the stock related to its Archegos margin calls on Friday, helping the firm avoid any losses in the episode

facts.claim: A jury convicted Archegos founder Bill Hwang in July 2024 of racketeering conspiracy, securities fraud, market manipulation and wire fraud after a nine-week trial; Judge Alvin Hellerstein sentenced him to 18 years in prison, and prosecutors said the scheme defrauded at least nine investment banks.
facts.quote: a jury convicted Hwang in July 2024 following a nine-week jury trial of racketeering conspiracy, securities fraud, market manipulation, and wire fraud

openQuestions: Site claim (Archegos entry) that Morgan Stanley sold about $5 billion of shares on the evening of March 25, 2021 and, with Goldman Sachs, moved early leaving Credit Suisse and Nomura with the biggest losses: supported by CNBC reporting.
Site claim that Morgan Stanley 'escaped with little or no loss': partly contradicted; Morgan Stanley reported $911 million of Archegos-related losses, though far less than Credit Suisse or Nomura.
Site claim that Credit Suisse lost 'about $5.5 billion': CNBC reported $4.7 billion initially and 'more than $5 billion' later; the exact figure should be checked against Credit Suisse filings.

Site claim (9/11 entry) that Poteshman 2006 and Chesney 2010 identified anomalous put spikes on Morgan Stanley: Poteshman's abstract does not name individual firms; Snopes notes reports of accelerated bets against Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch, while the SEC said it found no evidence of trading on advance knowledge. Chesney 2010 was not retrieved.
The site's claim that a March 25, 2021 prime-broker meeting ended without agreement was not covered by the sources returned.
